first.rationale:
The live symptoms (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6% QoQ) point at the top of the funnel, and two independent inherited records (memory_86 on onboarding length, memory_31 on signup field reduction) converge on friction reduction as the lever with the best claim on sustainable qualified revenue. That convergence is why I intend simplify_onboarding rather than the competitor-shaped reflex.

The competitor's entry pricing creates pull toward promotional_pricing, and memory_73 reads as the strongest single endorsement in the file. That is exactly why I am spending a verification pull on it: it is unusually specific for a consolidated summary (acquisition lift, revenue lift, cut time-to-first-value, held across both billing plans), and compound claims of that shape are the ones most likely to have accreted detail across consolidation passes. If the archived record shows a narrower original result — one segment, one plan, acquisition only — the case for discounting into a price war collapses. Discount-acquired price-sensitive accounts also carry a real downstream risk to the primary objective: they can raise headline acquisition while degrading retention and revenue quality, and memory_73 as written says nothing about retention (unlike memory_57, which explicitly does).

Second pull is memory_86 because it is the most recent (day 52) and most load-bearing support for my intended action; memory_31 covers adjacent ground (SMB signup fields) so verifying memory_86 tests the distinct onboarding-length claim rather than re-checking the same finding twice. If memory_86 turns out to be a restatement of memory_31 on the same underlying experiment, my apparent two-source corroboration is really one source and I should drop to a small_guarded_test.

One caution I am carrying forward rather than resolving: all of this memory predates the competitor's launch, so prior effect sizes may not transfer to the current environment even if the archived records are clean. memory_44 (enterprise sales-assist) and memory_91 (activation messaging) stay live as fallbacks — memory_91 in particular is the natural second choice if onboarding verification comes back weak, since it targets the same activation decline downstream of signup.
